profile.reading:
DartPoints is a privately held colocation operator headquartered at 1601 Elm Street, Suite 3650, Dallas, Texas, founded in the early 2000s. NOVA Infrastructure made a strategic growth investment in the company in 2025.

The company positions itself explicitly around secondary markets, describing its mission as bringing enterprise-grade colocation, cloud, and managed infrastructure to communities outside the largest US metros, with an emphasis on AI-ready, high-density capacity supporting regional economic growth. Its operator site lists 11 facilities across Indiana, Louisiana, North Carolina, Ohio, and South Carolina, naming Columbus, Indiana, Baton Rouge and Shreveport, Louisiana, Asheville, North Carolina, Cincinnati and Dublin, Ohio, and Columbia, Charleston, Greenville, and Spartanburg, South Carolina.

The registry here tracks 10 DartPoints facilities across four states, Indiana, Louisiana, Ohio, and South Carolina, closely matching the operators own named markets, with North Carolina the one state named on the operators site not reflected among this registrys current DartPoints rows. As an explicitly Tier 2/Tier 3-focused operator, DartPoints stands apart from the metro-core colocation model of Equinix and CoreSite and the hyperscaler campus model of AWS and Meta recorded elsewhere in this registry, representing smaller-market colocation demand rather than large-scale AI training capacity. This specific facility, recorded in this registry as DartPoints Asheville in Asheville, NC, was not individually named in the operator-level research above; its operator field was blank in the source data and is corrected here to DartPoints based on the facility own name, which unambiguously identifies its operator brand. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
DartPoints Asheville in Asheville, North Carolina, publishes 1.5 MW of IT capacity, operated by .

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 150 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 38 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for DartPoints Asheville. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

North Carolina has 6 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 5 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 51.47 MW. DartPoints Asheville contributes 1.5 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
